transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I honestly just can't see my studio or my life getting back on track anymore. It doesn't seem to matter how hard I work, or what kind of payment plan they put in front of me. I just don't see a way out of it.
When did you first start feeling this way—was it right around the time your business troubles began, or had you been feeling this way even before that?
Yeah, it was right around then. This has been going on since I took on the mortgage for the studio... so that was a little over two years ago. I'd say it's been about two years and two months now.
Over these past two years, has this low mood been pretty much constant day after day, or have you had stretches where you felt back to your normal self before it returned?

It's been pretty much constant. I haven't really had any stretches of feeling normal. Most days, I just... I wake up and there's already this heavy, gray feeling sitting on me. Even when I go into the shop, surrounded by the wood I used to love working with, it all just feels flat. I actually have to fight with myself to not just stand there staring at nothing. So, yeah, it's been like that day after day.

Over these past two years, has your mood ever gotten noticeably worse for a period of two weeks or more—so much that it affected your ability to work or function more than usual—or has it stayed at about the same level the whole time?

No, I wouldn't say it's ever taken a sharp dive like that. It's just... it's been exactly the same level of bad this whole time. Just a steady, heavy feeling, day in and day out. There hasn't been any specific couple of weeks where it suddenly got worse. It's just always there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a chronic, low-grade depressive mood present for over two years (2 years and 2 months), occurring most of the day, more days than not, without any distinct symptom-free intervals exceeding two months. There is no history of a discrete major depressive episode with acute worsening over a two-week period, nor any manic or hypomanic symptoms.
